previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for post-procedural observation following his fourth transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for residual liver tumors. The procedure was performed successfully under image guidance, targeting tumors in multiple liver segments using Oncozene beads. He tolerated the intervention well with no immediate complications and remained stable throughout the brief admission. His cirrhosis, diabetes, coronary disease, and other comorbidities were managed with continuation of home medications, including diuretics, antivirals, nadolol, and rifaximin. He was monitored for post-embolization syndrome but required no pain medication. Antibiotic prophylaxis was administered, with a course of oral ciprofloxacin prescribed at discharge. He was discharged home in good condition with instructions to monitor for fever or pain, continue all medications, and follow up with his liver specialist in two weeks.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  HCC.  Reviewed in liver tumor conference ___

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to MR abdomen performed for ___.

TECHNIQUE:   OPERATORS: Dr. ___ radiology fellow) and Dr.
___ radiology attending) performed the procedure.   Dr.
___ radiologist, personally supervised the trainee during the key
components of the procedure and reviewed and agreed with the trainee's
findings.

ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
125 mcg of fentanyl and 2.5 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 105 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.

MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl, Versed, lidocaine, 30 mg of Toradol, 3 g of Unasyn

CONTRAST: 110 ml of Optiray contrast.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  32.9 min, 464 mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Right common femoral artery access.
2. Common hepatic arteriogram with cone beam CT.
3.  Right hepatic arteriogram.
4.  Right hepatic arterial embolization with doxorubicin-loaded Oncozene
drug-eluting beads.
5.  Left hepatic arteriogram with cone beam CT.
6. Right common femoral arteriogram
7. Deployment of Angio-Seal arterial closure device

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent for the procedure and
chemotherapy was obtained from the patient/from the healthcare proxy/using an
interpreter.  The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol.  Both groins were prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Using palpatory and fluoroscopic guidance, the right common femoral artery was
punctured using a micropuncture set at the level of the mid-femoral head. A
0.018 wire was passed easily into the vessel lumen. A small skin incision was
made over the needle. Then the inner dilator and wire were removed and a
___ wire was advanced under fluoroscopy into the aorta. The micropuncture
sheath was exchanged for a 5 ___ sheath which was attached to a continuous
heparinized saline side arm flush.

A C2 glide Cobra catheter was advanced over ___ wire into the aorta. The
wire was removed and the celiac artery was selectively cannulated and a small
contrast injection was made to confirm position.  The Cobra catheter was
advanced into the common hepatic artery over a glidewire. The glidewire
removed and hand injection of dilute contrast confirmed positioning. A common
hepatic arteriogram was performed. A STC microcatheter pre-loaded with a
double angled wire was used to access the right hepatic artery and a right
hepatic hand injection arteriogram was performed.  Second order right hepatic
arterial embolization was performed with approximately 35% of the 100 mg of
dose of doxorubicin-loaded onto 1 vial 100 micron Oncozene drug-eluting beads.

The micro catheter was withdrawn and the Cobra catheter was advanced into the
left hepatic artery over the glidewire. Hand injection dilute contrast
confirmed position. Left hepatic arteriogram with cone beam CT was performed.
The STC microcatheter pre-loaded with a double angle wire was then used to
access the left hepatic artery.  Attempts to advance the wire into the third
order left hepatic artery thought to be partly supplying the right hepatic
dome lesion was unsuccessful and the further attempts to treat this branch was
aborted.

CONE-BEAM CT:  First, a rotational cone beam CT was performed with the
catheter in the common hepatic artery, to delineate the hepatic arterial
anatomy and blood supply to the tumor.  Multiplanar CT images were
reconstructed and 3D volume-rendered images of the arterial anatomy required
post-processing on an independent workstation by the attending physician, ___.
___.  After the initial superselective treatment of the Segment VIII lesion,
a second cone-beam CT was performed from the LHA.  This was done as the
initial cone-beam CT and angiogram suggested that some additional tumor supply
arose from a small branch of the LHA but the exact feeding branch could not be
definitely identified.  The cone-beam CT was essential in evaluating LHA
supply to the Segment VIII tumor.  Multiplanar CT images were reconstructed
and 3D volume-rendered images of the arterial anatomy required post-processing
on an independent workstation by Dr. ___.  These images were used in the
interpretation and reporting of this procedure.

All materials used in chemotherapy delivery were disposed of per departmental
protocol. A common femoral arteriogram was performed prior to use of a closure
device. Manual pressure was held until hemostasis was achieved.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.

FINDINGS: 

1. Conventional hepatic arterial anatomy .
2. Pre-embolization arteriogram showing tumor blush in hepatic segment VIII.
3. Cone-beam CTs showing hepatic segment VIII tumor predominately supplied by
the right hepatic artery though there is question of additional left hepatic
arterial supply
4.  Post-embolization showing staining of tumors in hepatic segment VIII.
5. Left hepatic arteriogram and cone beam CT demonstrating tiny additional
supply to hepatic segment VIII tumor
6. Right common femoral arteriogram demonstrating anatomy compatible with
arterial closure device

IMPRESSION: 

Successful right common femoral artery approach trans-arterial
chemoembolization of hepatic segment VIII tumor.

RECOMMENDATION:  Followup imaging in 1 month.
